1  JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 09.08.2019 at about 10.45 a.m., the Petitioner was riding the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EH-1421 from Kareenapalya towards Kanakapura road on the extreme left side of the road slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations reached near Liberty Apartment, Bengaluru City, at that time, the rider of TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HM-5361 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) came from opposite side i.e., from Kanakapura towards Kareenapalya in rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right i.e., wrong side,
dashed against the Petitioner's aforesaid vehicle.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to nearby Rithu Hospital for first aid treatment and then to Astra Hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent treatment as stated in the petition.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.

Prior to the date of accident, Petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as General Manager in Purvankara Constructions and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month and maintaining his family members.
He is the only earning member in the family and due to accidental injuries, he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent has appeared before the court through his counsel and filed the written statement.

He has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
He is the owner of the offending vehicle and it was used for delivery of provisions and it was always driven slowly and cautiously by following traffic rules.

He has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
On all these grounds, he has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding his Honda Activa bearing No.KA-41-EH-1421 on 09.08.2019 about 10.45 a.m. near Liberty Apartment, 80 Feet Road, Bengaluru District due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of TVS XL bearing No.KA-05-HM-5361?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?

7. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 09.08.2019 at about 10.45 a.m., he was riding the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EH-1421 from Kareenapalya towards Kanakapura road on the extreme left side of the road slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations reached near Liberty Apartment, Bengaluru City, at that time, the rider of TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HM-5361 came from opposite side i.e., from Kanakapura towards Kareenapalya in rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right i.e., wrong side, dashed against the Petitioner's aforesaid vehicle.
Due to the accident, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

9. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 8 and 16 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, seizure mahazar,
wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet and order sheet in CC.2325/2020.
As per wound certificate petitioner has sustained head, facial and chest injuries.
10. The respondent No.2 has contended that the vehicle of the petitioner has not sustained any injuries.
The petitioner was riding his vehicle with out following the traffic rules and regulation and suddenly came in front of offending vehicle which was left side of the road.
The respondent suddenly applied brake so avoid the accident, however the petitioner could not control his vehicle and thereby he dashed against the offending vehicle.
The police have filed a charge sheet against the Respondent mechanically without ascertaining the true facts.
The alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle 11.
Keeping in view of the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the respondent once again I have perused the material available on record.
Ex.P.7 IMV report shows that either of the vehicles have not sustained any damages.

However on perusal of the charge sheet, complaint and FIR, prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and not on the part of petitioner.
Neither the respondent has challenged the charge sheet before any authority nor rebut the evidence lead by the petitioner.

sentences.text: By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
There is no materials to disbelieve or rebut the evidence of the petitioner.
and charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2:-
As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained head,facial and chest injuries and the doctor opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
14. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Rithu hospital thereafter he shifted to Astra Hospital and he admitted as an inpatient from 9.8.2019 to 31.8.2019.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as general manager in Purvankara construction and was earning Rs 1,00,000/- Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

15. The Petitioner has examined Dr.Shailesh A V rao, Neuro Surgeon at St John's Medical hospital,
Bengaluru as PW-4 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.21 to 23.

Further, Billing and insurance Manager, Astra Super Speciality Hospital was examined as PW2 and has produced 3 documents at EX P9 to EX P11 and Medical Record Officer at Astra hospital Bengaluru was examined as PW-3 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.13 to 15.
16. PW-4

has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated at Astra Super Speciality hospital, Bengaluru and Petitioner has sustained lacerated wounds over glabella, right supra clavicular region, upper lip and left angle.
CT brain revealed contusions over left temporal and both parietal lobes, fractures of mandible and right zygoma.
He was intubated and connected to a mechanical ventilator.
On 10-08-2019 he underwent surgery for facio maxillary injuries.
On 13-08-2019 he underwent tracheostomy.
With treatment he gradually improved.
Further he has stated that due to said injuries he is unable to resume his work as a General Manager in a private construction.
He has impaired memory and intelligence.
His IQ was 49 (normal 90-109).
This is suggestive of moderate mental retardation and is below average in thinking and reasoning.
His frontal and parietal lobes were inadequate in functioning.

On IDEA, he obtained a score of 09,
suggestive of 40-70% disability.
MMSE was done on 13-03-2024 and he obtained a low score of 16/30.
His disability under Sec.E(11.1) amounts to a MRS Score of 2.
This amounts to a total disability of around 45%.
This disability is pertaining to whole body and is likely to be permanent.

17. During the course of cross-examination PW-4 has stated that he has not taken the test mentioned in Ex.P.22 neuro- psychological assessment report and he has taken the test mentioned in Ex.P.23 mini mental state examination.
Further he stated that he has assessed the disability on the basis of clinical examination.
18. It is pertinent to note that as admitted by PW-4, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

sentences.text:
Therefore considering injuries sustained by the petitioner as mentioned in the wound certificate and medical documents, this tribunal is of the opinion that PW2 did not treat the petitioner at any point of time, however considering the grievous injuries is on the head and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-4 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner,
the functional disability is assessed at 15%.
19. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 50 years and in the wound certificate it was mentioned age of the petitioner as 48 years.
Ex . P.24

Aadhar card shows that he was born on 6/4/1971, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 49 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 13.
20.
The age of the petitioner is 49 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
he was taken to Rithu hospital thereafter he shifted to Astra Hospital and he admitted as an inpatient from 9.8.2019 to 31.8.2019.
again from 31/8/2019 to 23/09/2019 and again from 24- 12-2020 to 26-12-2020 i.e, for a period of 48 days.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as General Manager in Purvankara Constructions and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
21. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2019, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 14,000/- Per Month.

Thus, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
22.
The petitioner was aged about 49 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 13.
The notional income taken as Rs 14,000 x 12 x 13 x 15/100= Rs.3,27,600/- towards loss of future income.
23. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and he admitted as an inpatient from 9.8.2019 to 31.8.2019.
again from 31/8/2019 to 23/09/2019 and again from 24-12-2020 to 26-12-2020 i.e, for a period of 48 days.
The period of 48 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
24. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
25. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced initially bill No.2 and 3 for amount of Rs.9,73,886/- at Ex.P.20.

Thereafter the petitioner summoned the bill accountant and he has produced medical bills Laveesha Kumar A.K vs Narasingh Ram on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199509172/
5 at Ex.P.10 as bill No.1 to 3 for amount of Rs.11,55,457.62 pertaining to the petitioner.

sentences.text: The Respondent has not seriously disputed the medical bills.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of .11,55,457/- towards Medical Expenses.
26. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.17-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Astra Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he admitted as an inpatient from 9.8.2019 to 31.8.2019.
again from 31/8/2019 to 23/09/2019 and again from 24-12-2020 to 26-12-2020 i.e, for a period of 48 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .50,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
27. Loss of earning during laid up period: With regard to loss of earnings during treatment.
He admitted as an inpatient from 9.8.2019 to 31.8.2019.
again from 31/8/2019 to 23/09/2019 and again from 24-12-2020 to 26-12-2020 i.e, for a period of 48 days.

He was admitted in the hospital multiple times and was undergoing treatment nearly for 2 months and hence loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 4 months and around 4 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 4 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .14,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .14,000 x 4 =
56,000/-.
28.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings  3,27,600/-
2. Pain and Sufferings  50,000/-
3. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
4. Medical expenses  11,55,457/-
5. Conveyance, Food,  50,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges 6. Loss of income during laid  56,000/-
 up period  Total  16,64,057/-
29. Liability: Respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
30. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.16,64,057/- together with interest @ 6%
